Subject: Access controls follow-up / clarification

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A few quick follow-ups from our security and engineering teams as we scope the pilot: 

- Can you confirm how Redwood enforces RBAC for customer data (roles, role-mgmt UI vs. API)?
- What are the break-glass procedures for emergency access by Redwood engineers? How is that audited?
- Data residency: we need EU-only storage for certain workloads (eu-west-1). Is that available for Dedicated/Private deployment?
- Retention & logging: what are default retention windows for request/response logs and KV cache, and can we extend/shorten them?

Some of these are blockers for our security review. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call next week if easier.

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara —

Great questions — thanks for laying these out. Quick recap + next steps below. I've attached a short RBAC diagram and our most recent SOC2 report for your review.

TL;DR answers:
- RBAC: role-based access with hierarchical roles; role management via Console UI + API. Customers can define custom roles and map to org-level groups (we support SCIM provisioning).
- Break-glass: emergency access is performed via a documented ticket + approval workflow, requires two-person auth for support engineers, and is fully auditable (immutable audit log entries + exported event artifacts).
- Data residency: EU regions are supported on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted API we can route EU traffic to eu-west-1 on request for enterprise plans.
- Retention/logging: default request/response logs retained 90 days; configurable per-customer (30/90/365) for Dedicated and Private. KV cache is ephemeral by default; customers can opt into longer persistence if needed.

Attachments: SOC2-report-Redwood-2025.pdf, RBAC-diagram.png

Next steps: can you confirm which of the above items are hard blockers vs. discussion items? If helpful, David can join a technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed. Proposed times: Tue 10-11am or Wed 2-3pm (CEST).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up / clarification

Sara — quick technical notes to expand on Marissa's summary. Marking the items we typically see as most relevant during security reviews.

1) RBAC and provisioning:
- Roles: Admin, Analyst, Developer, Support (least-privilege by default).
- Role management: via Console (GUI) and REST API; SCIM integration available for automatic sync.
- Fine-grained object ACLs: customers can scope access to projects/models/environments.

2) Support access / break-glass:
- Support engineers do NOT have persistent key access to customer plaintext data.
- Break-glass requires a support ticket, justification, and approval by the on-call manager + customer-designated approver (two-person rule).
- All break-glass events create an immutable record: who requested, approver, time, TTL of access, and session recordings for higher-risk requests.

3) Key management & encryption:
- Data encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) on Private deployments; hosted can integrate with KMS (AWS KMS/HSM).

4) Logging & retention:
- Request/response logs (metadata + full payload when enabled) retention configurable: default 90d; options 30/90/365d.
- Audit logs: immutable, stored in append-only buckets; can be exported to S3/GCS for long-term retention.

5) Data residency:
- Dedicated & Private: selectable region (eu-west-1 supported).
- Hosted: enterprise routing available with contractual controls.

I'll attach a sample RBAC policy template and an example break-glass SOP for reference. Happy to walk through on the follow-up call.

Attachments: RBAC-policy-examples.docx

—David

Thanks Marissa and David — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from Legal/Infra: 

- For break-glass sessions, how long do temporary credentials last? Can we require session recordings for any session that accesses PII?
- Is the two-person approval configurable so that we can require a named approver from our side for certain scopes?
- For Hosted routing to eu-west-1: will logs/audit data also be stored in EU? We need proof for our DPO.

If you can answer the above and share the SOC2 link, we can move to propose a pilot NDA and mutual action plan. We prefer to run the pilot in eu-west-1.

Sara
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Johnson <sara.johnson@fintrust.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up / clarification

Hi Sara —

Answers inline: 
- Temporary credentials: break-glass TTLs are configurable; default is 8 hours, we can shorten to 1 hour for PII-scoped sessions. Session recordings and elevated-privilege session capture are available and can be required via policy for PII access.
- Named approver: yes — customers can configure an allowlist of named approvers for certain scopes; the approval workflow will enforce that.
- Hosted EU routing: when routed to eu-west-1 we ensure logs/audit data remain in-region. We can provide a data flow diagram and DPO-facing statement in our security pack (link below).

Next steps I'll take this week: share secure SOC2 link and a short mutual action plan template for the pilot (NDA -> Security review -> Pilot in eu-west-1 -> evaluation). Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical deep-dive with David + Neha on Tue Jul 6 09:00-09:30 CEST — does that work for you?
